titulo: Work and introducing yourself professionally: Describing what you do

aula.objetivo: Name jobs and workplaces, say what you do, and handle a short job interview in the formal «Lei» way of speaking. Leave out the article in «Sono insegnante», use the reflexive «mi occupo di» and «mi sono laureata», and use «da» + the present for a job that is still going on, but «per» + the passato prossimo for a job that has ended. Avoid the English-speaker traps: «per» after «cercare» and «ho» with a reflexive verb.

itens.pt: to deal with, to be in charge of

blocos.titulo: What you do: «mi occupo di», «lo stipendio» and «il collega»
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: «occuparsi di» is a reflexive verb followed by «di»: «Mi occupo di vendite» (I deal with sales). STEP 2: a reflexive verb always needs its pronoun: «mi occupo», «ti occupi», «si occupa». The sentence «Occupo di vendite» is missing the «mi». STEP 3: «lo stipendio» takes «lo» because «st-» is «s» + a consonant. STEP 4: «il collega» ends in «-a» but it is masculine. For a woman it is «la collega». The plural is «i colleghi» for men and «le colleghe» for women. STEP 5: «il capo» is the boss. STEP 6: «la riunione» is a meeting at work, and it is feminine. STEP 7: «lo stipendio» is a salary. It looks like «stipend», but a stipend is usually a small fixed allowance.
blocos.comparacao: English says «I deal with sales» or «I work in sales», and an English speaker may drop the «mi» and say «occupo di vendite». Italian needs the reflexive pronoun. English also has no gender for «colleague», and it tells a man from a woman only by context. In Italian the same noun «collega» is shared by both, with «il» or «la» showing the gender, and an English speaker may turn «collega» into «collego» because most masculine nouns end in «-o».

erros.motivo: Before «s» + a consonant the article is «lo»: «lo stipendio».
«Collega» is a masculine noun that ends in «-a», so it does not change to «-o».
«Occuparsi» is reflexive and needs the pronoun «mi».

itens.enunciado: Which sentence says that you deal with sales?
itens.explicacao: The reflexive pronoun «mi» and the preposition «di» are both needed.
«St-» is «s» + a consonant, so the article is «lo».

itens.enunciado: What is a male colleague called?
itens.explicacao: «Collega» is masculine even though it ends in «-a».
With «mi» the verb is in the first person: «mi occupo».

itens.enunciado: Put in order: «Mi occupo di vendite»

blocos.enunciado: Say six sentences aloud about your work: what you deal with, who your boss and colleagues are, and when your meetings are.
Say aloud the phrase «mi occupo di» and the three words «lo stipendio», «il collega» and «la collega».
